profile.campus: Secaucus / North Bergen, Hudson County, New Jersey (Equinix New York metro campus)
profile.reading:
Per Equinix own site, this NY2 facility is located at 275 Hartz Way, Secaucus, NJ 07094 and totals 131,040 sq ft. Redundancy: N+1 Power redundancy, N+1 Cooling redundancy. No MW power capacity figure is published on this page.

Equinix's wider New York/New Jersey metro, anchored by this Secaucus-area campus, comprised nine data centers totaling roughly 739,000 square feet of technical space as of a 2026 Data Center Frontier report, which also detailed the neighboring NY5 building's history: built in 2012 and expanded in 2016 to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity, with four utility feeder lines and eight 2.5-megawatt backup generators, and the campus remained operational for a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. The campus houses matching engines for major stock-exchange electronic trading and serves financial-services firms seeking proximity to Wall Street with far more colocation space than Manhattan itself can offer; nearby NY11 in Carteret, NJ primarily serves Nasdaq and was being expanded to host an AWS Local Zone as of the same report.

Equinix, the operator, was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection provider operating more than 260 data centers across over 70 metros worldwide; the company converted to a real estate investment trust (REIT) in 2015. Within its International Business Exchange (IBX) portfolio, buildings like this one offer private cages and suites, Equinix Fabric software-defined interconnection, Internet Exchange peering, and cross-connects linking enterprises directly to cloud on-ramps for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud.

This Secaucus/North Bergen cluster sits in Hudson County, New Jersey, roughly 10 miles from Lower Manhattan; the area's lower real estate costs and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor, rather than any single anchor tenant, are what have concentrated Equinix's largest East Coast metro campus here rather than in New York City itself.

reading.body:
NY2 is a 131,040 square-foot building in the Secaucus area of Hudson County, New Jersey, roughly 10 miles from Lower Manhattan. Equinix publishes N+1 power and cooling redundancy for the site but does not publish a megawatt capacity figure for NY2 itself. The facility is part of a nine-building New York metro campus that Equinix describes as serving major financial, media, and enterprise companies, with particular strength in electronic trading infrastructure and cloud on-ramps.

The Secaucus campus clusters in a region where 48 data center facilities have been mapped statewide, of which only 5 publish power capacity figures. Among those five published figures totaling 111.3 megawatts across New Jersey, this campus ranks sixth. The neighboring NY5 building, built in 2012 and expanded in 2016, offers 20 megawatts of critical power capacity with four utility feeder lines and eight 2.5-megawatt backup generators, and the campus as a whole remained operational for a full week during Superstorm Sandy without grid power. Without a published figure for NY2 specifically, its ability to host AI training workloads cannot be estimated from operator data alone.

NY2's value to AI deployment depends on grid access and real estate cost rather than published specifications. The campus sits on the densest financial-services colocation land on the US East Coast outside Manhattan, with established utility relationships and proximity to Wall Street data flows. For operators constrained by real estate cost and grid feeder availability rather than building square footage, this location matters; for those seeking maximum compute density or published power guarantees, the lack of a published capacity figure means NY2 must be evaluated against other options with transparent specifications.
